subject: Regional capacity SKU mapping + preliminary sizing for Helix Labs renewal
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@helixlabs.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: platform-planning@helixlabs.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning - regional dedicated pools (US / APAC ask)

Laura —

Hope youre well. Our renewal conversation is underway and we want to scope dedicated capacity across regions for the next 12 months. Key asks from our infra/planning team:

- Baseline steady-state for model inference: ~12k qps across US (primarily us-west/us-east) with diurnal spikes up to 25k for a 4-hour window.
- APAC footprint: Singapore edge plus minimal EU failover; expected steady 2.5k qps, spikes to 6k during marketing events.
- Target latency: P99 < 200ms for production traffic.
- Hard constraint: data residency in EU for some customers (wed prefer EU pool for EU traffic).

Can Redwood provide a first-pass SKU mapping and rough node count per region (GPU type, reserved vs burst) so we can model TCO in our procurement review? Wed like this by end of week to share with finance.

Thanks — happy to take a short call if helpful.

Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Engineering
Helix Labs

Attachments: [detailed-traffic-profiles.csv]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:55:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning - regional dedicated pools (Helix) — preliminary sizing

Laura —

Attached is a quick model (hl_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) and a short summary below. Assumptions: modern 80B open model family, GPT-like autoregressive workloads, average prompt-to-response token length consistent with their traffic profile. Were assuming mixed precision (AMP) quantized FP16/INT8 paths for production.

Summary (first-pass):
- US (steady 12k qps, spikes 25k): recommend two dedicated reserved pools:
  - US-Reserved-XL: 32x A10G-equivalent nodes (or 16x H100-lite equivalent) for steady baseline — covers 80% of steady traffic with conservative KV cache assumptions.
  - US-Burst: 12x H100-p4x nodes pooled as burst capacity for the 4-hour spike windows. Burst configured as pay-for-burst with warm start.
- APAC (steady 2.5k, spikes 6k):
  - APAC-Reserved-M: 6x A10G-equivalent nodes for steady state.
  - APAC-Burst: 4x H100-p4x nodes for event spikes.
- EU (failover / residency):
  - EU-failover-min: 4x A10G-equivalent nodes; reserved but capacity kept minimal and used for EU-residency routing.

Estimated committed GPU equivalents (reserved): US 32 + APAC 6 + EU 4 = 42 A10G-equivalent nodes. Burst pool as 16 H100-class equivalents.

Notes / caveats:
- Latency target: with continuous batching and prefix caching we can be at P99 ~180ms in US for steady traffic. During cold burst startup P99 can exceed 200ms unless we reserve warm burst nodes (recommended).
- If they want strict P95/P99 SLAs during spikes, we should move a portion of burst into reserved capacity or add pre-warm windows.
- Pricing impact: H100-class burst is ~2.5x cost of A10G-equivalent; pricing proposal needs blended rates.

I attached the spreadsheet with qps-to-node mappings and a sensitivity tab (token length, batching window, KV hit rate).

- Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [hl_capacity_model_v1.xlsx]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning - regional dedicated pools (Helix) — ops + SLA notes

Laura / Team — quick operational notes to include when we share:

- Warm vs cold start: we should recommend a hybrid — reserve enough nodes to keep the critical 50% of spike traffic warm, and offer burst attach for the remainder. This keeps P99 < 200ms consistently while controlling cost.
- Deployment cadence: we can provision US reserved pool within 4 weeks after PO; APAC provisioning typically 6-8 weeks (hardware channel, region capacity). EU failover in 3-4 weeks but depends on customer KMS setup for residency.
- Redlines / procurement: Helix will need SOC2 evidence, IP allowlists, and a statement of data residency. We should bundle a short Ops playbook (runbooks + warm-up schedule) in the renewal packet.
- Attachment: sku_mapping_draft.pdf (high level SKU mapping, billing model options: strictly reserved vs hybrid).

Marissa
Head of Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira@helixlabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning - regional dedicated pools (US / APAC ask)

Samira —

Thanks for the traffic profile. Attached are two artifacts: a first-pass capacity model (hl_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) and a SKU/ops mapping (sku_mapping_draft.pdf). High level proposed plan:

1) US: hybrid reserved + burst approach. Reserve 32 A10G-equivalent nodes to cover baseline, add a 12-node H100-class burst pool with warm-start windows aligned to your 4-hour spike.
2) APAC: reserve 6 A10G-equivalent nodes, 4 H100-class burst for event spikes.
3) EU: 4-node reserved failover for residency; can be scaled up if Helix identifies EU customers that need steady capacity.

Operational items / next steps:
- We recommend a short working session next Tue (30 min) with your infra + our Ops to agree warm-window timing and KMS plan.
- Marissa will prepare an Ops playbook and SOC2/ residency checklist; Karthik will finalize node-to-qps mapping based on token-length scenarios.
- If Helix wants stricter P99 during bursts, we can shift 4 burst nodes into reserved in the first tranche. That will increase committed cost but guarantee latency.

Would you like us to turn this into a formal renewal addendum / capacity exhibit for PO review?

Best —
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [hl_capacity_model_v1.xlsx, sku_mapping_draft.pdf]
